SMTO-CFG-0032 — The model server address isn't a valid web address

GUID: 92869dc2-29f0-457e-ac6c-63cd2d82cc44
Slug: llm-endpoint-invalid
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • The address SMTO uses to reach your AI model is incomplete or mistyped: it may be missing http://, the server name, or have a port number outside 1 to 65535.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing. In the Main connection, make the Endpoint a full address such as http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1, then select Save Main. SMTO needs http:// or https://, a server name or IP address, and an optional port number from 1 to 65535.
  2. Select Check saved model to confirm SMTO can reach the address you just saved. It tests the saved address, so you know the fix took effect before you start new work.
  3. If this message was printed as a warning in the window where SMTO was started, ask the person who manages SMTO to fix the base_url line under llm in SMTO's startup settings file (usually config.yaml). That startup check reads the file, not Model routing, so the address must be corrected there too.

What success looks like

  • After you select Check saved model, its result appears with no error, and new Tasks start normally.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change unrelated settings such as timeouts or limits; they won't fix an address problem.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Model endpoint parsing rejected the configured or requested base URL because the host was empty, the scheme was not http or https, the URL was malformed, or the port was not an integer from 1 to 65535.

What this means

  • Model endpoint parsing rejects a missing host, malformed URL/port or a scheme outside HTTP(S), with explicit port restricted to 1–65535. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Model endpoint parsing rejects a missing host, malformed URL/port or a scheme outside HTTP(S), with explicit port restricted to 1–65535.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the effective base URL versus host/scheme/port inputs; no network connection is attempted by this validation.

How to fix it

  • Correct the endpoint where it comes from: the Main (or Helper) endpoint in Model routing, which is copied into each request's llm_base_url; llm_base_scheme/host/port/path overrides sent to /api/agent/model/config or /api/agent/runtime-controls; or llm.base_url in the bootstrap YAML read by the advisory startup.sh preflight (python -m agent_runtime.api.llm_health, skipped when AOR_LLM_PREFLIGHT_ENABLED=0). It must parse as an http(s) URL with a host and a port of 1-65535; then confirm reachability separately.
  • Set the intended model endpoint using http or https, a valid host and a port from 1 to 65535. Confirm its certificate and service identity before refreshing models.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended endpoint parses correctly and a separate trusted health check can run.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
